newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Prompt offers weigh down diesel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Prompt offers weigh down diesel.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were steady on Wednesday but prompt offers were weighing heavily on values with support seen for late June cargoes, traders said on Wednesday.
Offers for cargoes loading June 12-16 were heard at a low of $24.80 per barrel free-on-board Singapore with a total of three 150,000 barrel offers seen for these prompt cargoes.
A 150,000 barrel cargo traded at $25.00 per barrel for May between two Japanese trading houses, with other sellers seen for similar loading dates at $25.10 and $25.20, traders said.
Traders said the low offers for prompt cargoes were mainly from sellers seeking to offload their surplus arbitrage cargoes.
"The pressure on the prompt market is strong because there are few end-users left for first half June cargoes," a trader said.
Traders said fundamentals remain bearish due to slow demand from China, with the run cuts at one Singapore refiner having a minimal impact on the market.
Looking toward the Indian tender to buy July delivery cargoes, to be awarded on Thursday, traders said Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is not expected to buy much.
IOC is expected to award between 400,000 tonnes to 600,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery in July, compared to 315,000 tonnes in June and 840,000 in May.
Traders said offers into the tender were at very low levels, reflecting sellers' desperate search for markets.

Offers into the west coast of India for 1.0 percent sulphur grade diesel were heard around $1.00 per barrel over Mideast quotes on a cost and freight (c-and-f) basis for deliveries in the first week of July. Deliveries for later July were at $1.15-$1.35 per barrel over Mideast quotes c-and-f west coast.
Into the east coast of India, offers were quoted at between $1.90-$2.20 per barrel c-and-f basis.
Traders said Mideat related quotes for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel were about five cents more.
On Mediterranean related quotes, offers were around $14.50 per tonne premia into the west coast and at $21.80 per tonne premia for deliveries to the east coast.
Offers for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel were at $15.20 per tonne premia over Mediterranean quotes on a c-and-f basis to the west coast of India.
Sri Lanka has issued a tender to buy 220,000 barrels of diesel and 80,000 barrels of jet for delivery between June 21-22.
